soundness_flags.label: def:generic-identification, thm:component-radical-certificate, and oeq:generic-uniform-door-completeness
soundness_flags.one_line: Zariski density of each order's positive realizable cell does not ensure two generic orders are simultaneously realizable at any covariance point, so componentwise ideal comparisons can assert equality or return a same-covariance countermodel arc for orders that never share an observed-data fiber.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 1: assaad-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: Assaad's Theorem 10 ranges over all positive no-hidden-confounding linear SCM pairs with a shared order, whereas M_df additionally imposes invariant innovations and baseline-parent modular interventions; the stated hypotheses do not establish equality or the needed inclusion of compatible model classes, so the claimed exact reduction does not follow.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3, Assumption 1 and Definition 1; p. 6, Definition 4; p. 7, Assumption 3; p. 10, Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper restricts interventions to baseline-parent mechanisms with modular untouched mechanisms, defines inherited difference-edge directions and diff-separation, assumes regression equality iff diff-separation, and proves population LDiffPC has the true skeleton with only sound orientations.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PMLR PDF pp. 10 and 14; Definition 4, Theorem 10, Lemmas 11--13, and discussion of BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Under Assumptions 1--3, Theorem 10 characterizes direct-effect identification trivially or by a common single-door through C.1/C.2 and gives the partial-regression functional; the paper explicitly identifies the BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B direct effect under its conditions.
Proposition 2 obtains observable constraints by elimination, while Propositions 3--4 use a target-augmented parametrization and elimination Gröbner bases for generic identification testing.

The article studies coloured Gaussian DAG models with equality constraints on structural coefficients and error variances, including rational parametrization and model geometry; it does not supply paired LDiffPC completion theory.
The paper uses test inversion under single-environment equal-error-variance Gaussian structure uncertainty to form confidence sets for total causal effects.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion for MPDAGs, a graph-only setting without paired covariance-ledger constraints.

The half-trek criterion is polynomial-time sufficient for generic identification and is accompanied by a distinct necessary obstruction; it does not establish a paired-difference-graph treewidth algorithm.
The paper gives constructive complete adjustment and separator criteria for DAGs and ancestral graphs, not algebraic compatibility across paired covariance completions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Redefine generic identification and the radical test fiberwise: require a nonempty common positive semialgebraic realization cell for every compared pair of orders, and run numerator membership on its relevant component or a quantified common-fiber stratification.

Replace Proposition 1's exact Assaad reduction by a proved transfer statement: either establish that the Assaad-compatible class is represented by the stated baseline/invariant-noise class in the fully specified regime, or state only the valid sufficient-direction reduction.
Archive the full machine-readable A4 output—ledger inventory, prime components, common-real-fiber certificates, realizability checks, and target remainders—rather than only the displayed C-star row.

recommended_next_step: Revise the completion-fiber semantics and the Assaad special-case transfer, then rerun this novelty review before advancing to Stage 0.
